rules.notes: safe_harbor=true: Policy explicitly states 'In order to receive a monetary bug bounty payout (when applicable), you must provide your Testing IP address. This information is also required in order to fall within Adobe's Safe Harbor policy.' Safe harbor is explicitly offered, conditioned on providing your testing IP. | mass_scanning_allowed=false (safe default — policy says DO NOT cause DoS; no scanning permission granted). | automated_tools_allowed=false (safe default — not addressed in policy; DO NOT cause DoS language implies restriction). | bucket_listing_allowed=true (safe default — not addressed). | bucket_download_allowed=false (safe default — not addressed). | cve_age_min_days=30 (safe default — not specified). | requires_ownership_proof=true (safe default — policy requires testing IP for safe harbor; own-account-only testing stated explicitly). | IMPORTANT per-product notes: (1) Many desktop executables (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, etc.) are eligible for SUBMISSION but NOT for BOUNTY per CSV. (2) ColdFusion reports require testing against latest version with Lockdown installer — non-lockdown installs are OOS. (3) XXE in ColdFusion is temporarily OOS. (4) IMS OAuth vulnerabilities are temporarily OOS. (5) Learning Manager: Custom roles/Social Learning improper access controls and OAuth misconfigurations are temporarily OOS. (6) Express: express.adobe.com and express-embed.adobe.com are OOS (only new.express.adobe.com is in scope). (7) DoS/resource consumption is OOS unless it leads to sensitive memory disclosure. (8) Third-party endpoints (*.contentsquare.net, *.doubleclick.net, etc.) used by Photoshop Web are OOS. (9) Firefly: IDORs in backend API related to jobs/data with random UUID4 short-lived IDs are OOS. (10) Behance: public production site www.behance.net is OOS; only net.s2stagehance.com is in scope. (11) Acrobat Web OOS: *.adobesign.com (Adobe Sign Web production). (12) Rate limiting bypasses and race conditions are OOS for Acrobat Web unless significant security impact. (13) User-Agent string 'h1_username' is required during testing to be eligible for bounty.

raw_policy_excerpt:
Adobe recognizes that the security community is a force multiplier in our quest to provide a safe and secure experience for Adobe's customers. To that end, we welcome the contributions of security researchers and strive to provide the best vulnerability disclosure experience possible.

At the time of report submission, Adobe will request your "testing IP address". By providing your testing IP address, this will allow Adobe to conduct expedited incident response investigations by ruling your traffic out from valid adversary traffic. This will also help ensure your testing traffic is not blocked/interrupted while bug hunting.

In order to receive a monetary bug bounty payout (when applicable), you must provide your Testing IP address. This information is also required in order to fall within Adobe's Safe Harbor policy.

# Rules of Engagement
* DO include the User-Agent string `h1_username` while testing. This is a requirement in order to be eligible for a bounty.
* DO NOT use social engineering (e.g. phishing, vishing, smishing) techniques.
* DO NOT test existing customer environments without explicit permission from the owner.
* DO NOT cause a potential or actual denial of service of Adobe applications and systems.
* DO NOT use an exploit to view data without authorization or cause corruption of data.
* DO make a good faith effort to avoid privacy violations, destruction of data, and interruption or degradation of our service. Only interact with accounts you own or with the explicit permission of the account holder.

# Program Exclusions (partial)
- DoS / resource consumption testing unless it leads to sensitive memory disclosure
- Vulnerabilities in mobile applications relying on the installation of a malicious APK are out-of-scope
- Mobile app submissions that require the use of rooted or jailbroken devices will not be accepted
- Self-XSS
- Logout and other instances of low-severity Cross-Site Request Forgery(CSRF)
- Missing HTTP security headers
- Password and account recovery policies
- Missing best practices in SSL/TLS configuration
- Username / email enumeration via Login Page or Forgot Password Page
- Brute-forcing credentials
- Attacks requiring MITM or physical access
- Reports that only reference data listed on third-party breach or credential-dump services are out of scope unless the reporter can demonstrate the exposure originated from a vulnerability in Adobe systems.

# Terms and Conditions
- Please use your own account for testing or research purposes. Do not attempt to gain access to another user's account or confidential information.
- Do not store, share, compromise, or destroy Adobe or customer data. If PII is encountered, immediately halt your activity, purge related data, and contact Adobe.
- Do not engage in any activity that violates federal or state laws or regulations or the laws of any country where the researcher is conducting research activity.
- This program is not open to individuals who reside in Venezuela, Mainland China, Hong Kong, Russia, Belarus, Ukraine, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Crimea region of Ukraine, Sudan, or Syria.
